candidates.title: Grusch exposes covert UFO crash retrieval and reverse engineering program
candidates.quote:
Intelligence officer David grush hey man
hey who blew the cover on a covert
multi-decade long UFO crash retrieval
and reverse engineering program being
funded by American Tax pair dollars

link.reason: Both are about the same covert US legacy crash-retrieval program that Grusch says he uncovered and disclosed. The nearest story's tellings describe Grusch uncovering this same program.
link.difference: The host tells it second hand, crediting Grusch. He adds that the program ran for decades, reverse-engineered craft and was paid for with US taxpayer dollars, and he dates the disclosure to 2023.

candidates.title: Grusch brings 40 firsthand witnesses to the Intelligence Community Inspector General
candidates.quote:
importantly he's not alone he's brought
40 people who have handled exotic UFO
material firsthand to the intelligence
community's Inspector General

link.reason: Both tell of Grusch filing his Inspector General complaint and getting named witnesses interviewed by the IG in Washington around 2022, so this is the same event at the same grain.
link.difference: The host gives a count of 40 witnesses who handled exotic UFO material firsthand and names the Intelligence Community Inspector General, where the story's place is the DoD Inspector General and no number is given.

candidates.title: Grusch testifies under oath before Congress
candidates.quote:
it before I I didn't need this and he
testified about his findings under oath
in front of Congress this summer

link.reason: The telling and the story describe the same event: David Grusch testifying before Congress in Washington, D.C. in summer 2023, told by host Jesse Michels.
link.difference: This telling stresses that the testimony was given under oath and says it was about his findings, while the story's telling gives late July as the time.

candidates.title: FAA supervisor tracks five unknowns near Malmstrom; Hastings begins his research
candidates.quote:
Hastings worked there as a janitor in
high school in the 60s one night an FAA
supervisor casually mentioned to him
that he was tracking five unknowns on
his Scopes and called young Hastings
over to his desk to check them out

link.reason: The telling is about Hastings' own teenage experience: an FAA supervisor at Malmstrom showed him five unknowns on radar, and that is how his research began. The nearest story covers his whole body of interviews about UFOs at nuclear bases, which is wider. The 1967 Malmstrom story is a different event: missiles shut down, as told by Salas.

candidates.title: Hastings interviews 167 military sources on UFOs at nuclear sites
candidates.quote:
began a lifelong journey for Hastings
interviewing 100 167 US military sources
former or retired ICBM launch officers
missile maintenance security and radar
operators

link.reason: Both are about Robert Hastings' body of interviews about UFOs at US nuclear sites, the research collected in his book UFOs and Nukes. The telling covers the whole research effort, not one incident inside it.
link.difference: This telling gives a count of 167 US military sources, names their roles (ICBM launch officers, missile maintenance, security and radar operators), calls the interviews a lifelong journey and dates them from the 1960s onward rather than the 1940s.

candidates.title: 1954 Atomic Energy Act language written to protect UFO secrets
candidates.quote:
grush shows that the language of the
1954 atomic energy act which defines
which materials are subject to nuclear
secrecy was written in a sneaky but
deliberate way to protect our UFO
secrets too

link.reason: Both tellings make the same claim, credited to Grusch: that the Atomic Energy Act of 1954's definition of nuclear materials covers UFO crash material and so keeps it secret.
link.difference: The host relays it from Grusch and says the language was written deliberately and sneakily to protect UFO secrets, which is a stronger claim than Grusch's reading of what the definition covers.

candidates.title: UFO custody passed from Manhattan Project to AEC to Department of Energy clearance system
candidates.quote:
the Manhattan Project
would have custody of it and then it
would go into the atomic energy
commission and then it would go into the
department of energy which has its own
line of clearances

link.reason: Both are Jacques Vallee's account of the custody chain from the Manhattan Project to the AEC to the DOE's own clearance system, in almost the same words. The "it" in the telling is the craft the story names as the Trinity craft.
link.difference: This telling credits nobody, while the story's telling credits Paola Harris and Robert Oppenheimer; it also says only "UFO custody" from the 1940s on, without naming the Trinity craft or the year 1945.

candidates.title: Grusch: the Manhattan Project was the original UFO program
candidates.quote:
grush even told me in a
car ride in DC that the Manhattan
Project was basically the original UFO
program

link.reason: Both tellings claim, on Grusch's word, that the Manhattan Project was the first UFO program, the forerunner of Blue Book, in the 1940s United States.
link.difference: Told secondhand by Jesse Michels, who says Grusch told him in a car ride in DC. It leaves out the detail about colleagues' grandparents handling UFO reports.

candidates.title: Colleagues' grandparents were UFO report people on the Manhattan Project
candidates.quote:
there are some people I'm uh colleagues
with that like their grandparents were
actually you know the UFO report people
on the Manhattan Project

link.reason: This telling is the same as the first story. In both, David Grusch says colleagues of his had grandparents who were the UFO report people on the Manhattan Project, and the quote is almost word for word.

downgraded.why: a testimony telling and the program story manhattan-project-as-the-first-blue-book-colleagues-grandpar-1940: a program and a story of another kind are different grains

candidates.title: Edward Condon, atomic insider turned UFO debunker
candidates.quote:
then randomly he
pops back up in 1966 and his clearance
is mysteriously restored he's then
placed on a panel which deals a death
blow to UFO research claiming it's all a
waste of time and money

link.reason: The telling covers Condon's whole career, from Göttingen and Los Alamos through losing his clearance to its restoration in 1966 and his place on the UFO panel. The nearest stories each take one piece of that: his Manhattan Project work (1940s) and the Condon Committee's ties to the Air Force (1966-68). The career and one event in it are different grains.

candidates.title: Was Condon blackmailed by FBI agent Guy Hottel into debunking UFOs
candidates.quote:
blackmailed you see while being
investigated for communist sympathies in
the ' 50s a dossier of field reports was
being created on him in the background
by an FBI field agent named guy hoddle

link.reason: The nearest story is Condon's career arc from atomic insider to UFO debunker, which hints that his clearance was mysteriously restored. This telling makes one specific claim within that arc: that FBI agent Guy Hottel built a dossier on Condon during the 1950s communist investigation and used it to blackmail him into debunking UFOs. A separate theory inside a career story is a different grain, so it counts as a new story.

candidates.title: The 1952 Hottel memo on a crashed UFO with alien crew
candidates.quote:
hoddle is now famous for his 1952 hoddle
memo the most read document on the FBI's
website it describes an Air Force
officer writing to hoddle about a
crashed UFO with an alien crew inside of
it

link.reason: The telling is about the 1950 Hottel memo, a document about a crashed saucer and its crew. The nearest story is the theory that Hottel blackmailed Condon. That story names Hottel but makes a different claim about a different subject, so this is a different story. No other story is about the Hottel memo.

candidates.title: Lockheed Skunk Works response to Grusch's testimony

link.reason: The telling is about Lockheed Skunk Works' corporate statement in response to Grusch's 2023 testimony. The closest stories cover other parts of the testimony (gifted craft, the SCIF being denied) or other Lockheed episodes (Trimble rebuffing Cook), and none of them is about Lockheed's reaction.

candidates.title: Philadelphia Experiment ship teleportation
candidates.quote:
things like the Philadelphia Experiment

link.reason: None of the stories in the corpus is about the Philadelphia Experiment, the claimed teleportation of a ship and its crew from Philadelphia to Norfolk. The closest ones are about Townsend Brown's Navy career and his gravitator, which are separate events.

candidates.title: Brown's deliberate disinformation and electrogravitics in the B-2 bomber
candidates.quote:
intentionally created a lot of
disinformation about his work to protect
it he showed people his fluid dialectric
system that used ionic wind instead of
the solid dialectric gravitator we now
even know that the B2 stealth bomber
uses Brown's Electric gravitics

link.reason: Both have Jesse Michels claiming that the B-2 stealth bomber uses Townsend Brown's electrogravitics (the Biefeld-Brown effect). The telling's 'we now even know' points to the same claim the story attributes to the 1992 Aviation Week report.
link.difference: This telling credits Paul Schatzkin's The Man Who Mastered Gravity rather than Aviation Week, gives no date, and frames the B-2 claim with Brown's deliberate disinformation: he showed people an ionic-wind fluid-dielectric system instead of the solid-dielectric gravitator.

candidates.title: Townsend Brown forms NICAP
candidates.quote:
about UFOs he even formed the national

phenomena or nikat for short the first
civilian UFO study
group

link.reason: The telling and the story both have Jesse Michels saying Townsend Brown founded NICAP in the 1950s in the United States, and the story's title names that founding outright. It is the same claim at the same scope.
link.difference: This telling states the NICAP founding outright and calls it the first civilian UFO study group; the story's existing telling only mentions the gravitator looking like a saucer.

candidates.title: Wright-Patterson AFB: Roswell materials and anti-gravity research
candidates.quote:
Wright Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio
it's where the Roswell crash materials
were reportedly taken it becomes an
anti-gravity Research Center in the '
50s

link.reason: The telling and the story are both Jesse Michels's place-lore about Wright-Patterson AFB. Both say the base became an anti-gravity research center in the 1950s, so they make the same core claim about the same site and era.
link.difference: This telling adds that the Roswell crash materials were reportedly taken to Wright-Patterson in 1947, and it leaves out the nuclear test facility and the Blue Book role.

candidates.title: Curtis LeMay refuses access to the secret room at Wright-Patterson
candidates.quote:
I called Curtis lame and I

Wright Patterson where you put all this
secret
stuff can I go in there I've never heard

link.reason: Both describe the same incident: a senator asks Curtis LeMay for access to the secret room at Wright-Patterson and LeMay angrily cusses him out. The quote is nearly word for word the same.
link.difference: Here the unnamed politician tells it in the first person and adds that LeMay told him never to ask that question again. The story's telling is the host quoting the senator, with only a vague Cold War date.

candidates.title: JFK memo to CIA director McCone on unknowns, 10 days before his death
candidates.quote:

unknowns in space and it was written to

documents: JFK memo to John McCone, November 12, 1963

link.reason: Both tellings describe the same document: JFK's November 12, 1963 letter to CIA Director John McCone asking about unknowns/UFO data, said to have been released through FOIA, dated ten days before his death.
link.difference: This telling describes the letter as asking about "unknowns in space" and does not give the 2006 release year or credit an archivist.

candidates.title: E. Howard Hunt links JFK's death to UFO inquiries

another CIA

link.reason: The nearest story is the November 1963 JFK letter to McCone asking for UFO data, which is a document. This telling is a different claim: E. Howard Hunt's theory that JFK's assassination was partly tied to his UFO inquiries.

candidates.title: Congress members denied access to the SCIF
candidates.quote:
we
were denied access to the skiff

link.reason: Both tellings describe members of Congress in Washington, D.C. in 2023 being unable to get a SCIF for a classified briefing. This is the episode around Grusch's testimony. Here one of the members tells it firsthand.
link.difference: An unnamed speaker who appears to be one of the members tells it firsthand ("we were denied access") and says it more strongly as an outright denial of access, without naming Grusch; Grusch's telling says only that they couldn't reserve a SCIF.

candidates.title: Walter B. Smith 1953 letter on using the phenomenon for psychological warfare
candidates.quote:
letters like the one by CIA director
Walter B Smith in
1953 saying that we should use the
phenomena for psychological warfare
against the Soviets you have similar
leaked letters from Alan Dulles

link.reason: The closest story is the 1952 CIA memo. That memo calls UFOs a national security matter that could cause mass panic, and it credits no named author. This telling is a 1953 letter from Director Walter B. Smith proposing to use the phenomenon for psychological warfare against the Soviets, plus Dulles letters. As told, these are different documents making different claims.
